\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{لاغر} \fa{شدن} (lâghar shodan)}{لاغر شدن (lâghar shodan)}]{\fa{لاغر} \fa{شدن} (lâghar shodan) — to lose weight, to get thin}

\label{lesson:FA-C498-laghar-shodan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for the spine, then the Persian for a skull.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{لاغر} \fa{شدن}}
\textbf{\fa{لاغر} \fa{شدن}} (\emph{lâghar shodan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to lose weight, to get thin\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{با} \fa{ورزش} \fa{پنج} \fa{کیلو} \fa{لاغر} \fa{شد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{u bâ varzesh panj kilo lâghar shod.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He lost five kilos through exercise.
\end{quote}

\emph{lâghar} 'thin' + \emph{shodan} 'to become'; present stem \emph{shav-}. The opposite is \emph{châq shodan}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{lâghar} is an everyday Persian word for thin, but EtymDB has no entry for it, and its origin is not settled. \emph{shodan}, 'to become', is inherited.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lâghar shodan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lâghar shodan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{lâghar shodan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for the spine, then the Persian for a skull, then say \emph{lâghar shodan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{چاق} \fa{شدن} (châq shodan)}{چاق شدن (châq shodan)}]{\fa{چاق} \fa{شدن} (châq shodan) — to put on weight}

\label{lesson:FA-C498-chaq-shodan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a skull, then the Persian for to lose weight.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{چاق} \fa{شدن}}
\textbf{\fa{چاق} \fa{شدن}} (\emph{châq shodan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to put on weight\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{در} \fa{تعطیلات} \fa{کمی} \fa{چاق} \fa{شد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{u dar ta'tilât kami châq shod.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He put on a bit of weight over the holidays.
\end{quote}

\emph{châq} 'fat' + \emph{shodan}. \emph{châq} is blunt; \emph{topol} 'chubby' is kinder.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{châq} is often linked with a Turkic word, but EtymDB lists it without a source and its origin is not settled. \emph{shodan}, 'to become', is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{châq shodan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{châq shodan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a skull, then the Persian for to lose weight, then say \emph{châq shodan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{رژیم} \fa{گرفتن} (rezhim gereftan)}{رژیم گرفتن (rezhim gereftan)}]{\fa{رژیم} \fa{گرفتن} (rezhim gereftan) — to go on a diet}

\label{lesson:FA-C498-rezhim-gereftan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to lose weight, then the Persian for to put on weight.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{رژیم} \fa{گرفتن}}
\textbf{\fa{رژیم} \fa{گرفتن}} (\emph{rezhim gereftan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to go on a diet\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{مادرم} \fa{از} \fa{اول} \fa{ماه} \fa{رژیم} \fa{گرفته} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mâdaram az avval-e mâh rezhim gerefte ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My mother has been on a diet since the start of the month.
\end{quote}

\emph{rezhim} 'diet; regime' + \emph{gereftan} 'to take'; present stem \emph{gir-}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{rezhim} was borrowed from French \emph{régime}, 'rule, order', which EtymDB traces to Latin \emph{regimen} (EtymDB); Lewis \& Short gloss \emph{regimen} 'a guiding, a rule' (Lewis \& Short). \emph{gereftan}, 'to take', is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rezhim gereftan}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to lose weight, then the Persian for to put on weight, then say \emph{rezhim gereftan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{ویتامین} (vitâmin)}{ویتامین (vitâmin)}]{\fa{ویتامین} (vitâmin) — a vitamin}

\label{lesson:FA-C498-vitamin}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to put on weight, then the Persian for to go on a diet.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{ویتامین}}
\textbf{\fa{ویتامین}} (\emph{vitâmin}) — \textquotedblleft{}a vitamin\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{پرتقال} \fa{ویتامین} \fa{زیادی} \fa{دارد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{porteqâl vitâmin-e ziyâdi dârad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Oranges have a lot of vitamins.
\end{quote}

Plural \emph{vitâminhâ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{vitâmin} is a modern loan, usually traced to French \emph{vitamine}. EtymDB has no entry for the Persian word.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{چاقی} (châqi)}{چاقی (châqi)}]{\fa{چاقی} (châqi) — being overweight; obesity}

\label{lesson:FA-C498-chaqi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to go on a diet, then the Persian for a vitamin.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{چاقی}}
\textbf{\fa{چاقی}} (\emph{châqi}) — \textquotedblleft{}being overweight; obesity\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{چاقی} \fa{برای} \fa{قلب} \fa{خوب} \fa{نیست}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{châqi barâ-ye qalb khub nist.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Being overweight is bad for the heart.
\end{quote}

The noun from \emph{châq} 'fat' with \emph{-i}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{châqi} is built on \emph{châq}, 'fat', with the native noun ending \emph{-i}. The origin of \emph{châq} is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
